conviction_note: The findings roughly cancel (sum +0.25). Q3 originations were already published at $4,117.8m, 2.6% below Q2, which at Q2's take rate points to revenue about $355m against a $365m consensus. The FY guide ($1.4bn revenue, $294m adj. EBITDA) needs a steep Q4 step-up after a September Fed hike that a peer (Pagaya) blamed for take-rate compression. Against that: September per-day originations were the quarter's best, peer credit is benign, the stock sits at its 52-week low, and 33% of float is short. p_up 45 x abs_move 13 gives -1.3. The lean comes from this name's reaction function: 6 of its last 7 prints fell, and the Q2 beat with a reaffirmed guide went -0.4% and then drifted about -30%. That lean is set against the squeeze risk, which is why p_up is 45 and not lower. The sum of findings (+0.25) and the scaled number (-1.3) differ in sign; that gap is the reaction history, which no single finding carries.

findings.finding: Upstart pre-released Q3 2026 originations of $4,117.8m (Jul $1,397.4m, Aug $1,342.1m, Sep $1,378.3m), 2.6% below Q2's $4,227.2m. At Q2's fee take rate ($348.0m fees / $4,227.2m = 8.23%) that is about $339m of fees; adding Q2-like net interest and fair-value income of about $16m gives total revenue near $355m, about 2-3% below the $365m consensus, which sits flat on Q2. The 25bp Fed hike of 2026-09-16 also points to a negative fair-value mark on about $1.06bn of balance-sheet loans.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: originations $2.9bn against $3.3bn consensus and revenue $277m against $280m; the stock fell 14.8% (American Banker, 2025-11-05). Q2 2026: revenue $364.7m beat with the guide reaffirmed, and the stock went -0.4% on the day (baseline). Beats have not been paid; misses on volume have been punished.
findings.why_not_priced: Originations are public, but a consensus of $365.5m (Benzinga) / $364.6m (Earnings Whispers) is flat on Q2 revenue while volume fell 2.6% q/q. That requires the take rate to rise about 20bp after a quarter whose rise the CFO credited to seasonality and mix, while saying she expected 'relative stability'. If estimates had absorbed the volume release, consensus revenue would sit near $355m, not $365m. Partly priced: the stock has fallen about 10% since the 10-05 release.
findings.independence: Q2 fee and origination figures come from the Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001647639/000164763926000062/upst991prq22026.htm). The take-rate stability remark is the CFO's on the Q2 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15382707037168640). Peer read: Pagaya's Q3 release of 2026-10-29 reports a 91bp YoY fall in FRLPC as % of volume, attributed to 'the short-term impact of higher benchmark rates' (https://finviz.com/news/411281/pagaya-reports-third-quarter-2026-results). That is a proxy, not Upstart's own number.

findings.finding: The reaffirmed FY2026 guide needs a sharp H2 ramp. On revenue, $1.4bn less H1 $673m ($308m Q1 + $365m Q2) leaves $727m for H2. On adj. EBITDA, $294m less H1 $117.4m leaves $176.6m, against Q2's $76.9m. With Q3 volume down q/q and fixed costs guided up low single digits in Q3 and Q4, Q4 would need about $370m+ revenue and about $95m EBITDA. That makes a trim, or a guide hit only through an aggressive Q4, likely. The macro moved against the guide: the Fed hiked 25bp on 2026-09-16 (its first hike since 2023) and 12 of 18 officials project another by year-end. A direct peer, Pagaya, implied a Q4 volume midpoint about 14% below Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide-driven prints have produced this name's largest moves: Feb 2025 +31.8% on a strong initial guide; Aug 2025 -18.7% and Feb 2026 -15.0% on guide/take-rate disappointment (baseline). A reaffirm in Aug 2026 got -0.4% and then about -30% drift.
findings.why_not_priced: The Street's Q3+Q4 EBITDA ($83.2m + $93.9m = $177m) still equals the guide exactly, which means estimates are anchored to the company number rather than to the post-hike rate path. If a cut were priced, consensus would sit below the guide. The stock at its 52-week low with +16.8 put skew does show the market fears it, so part of this is in the price.
findings.independence: Fed hike and dot plot: https://investinglive.com/central-banks/fed-hikes-hints-at-more-7-takeaways-from-the-september-fomc/ (2026-09). Pagaya Q4 implied volume and take-rate compression: https://finviz.com/news/411281/pagaya-reports-third-quarter-2026-results (2026-10-29). Shares the Q2 8-K with finding 1, but this one rests on the guide arithmetic, not the Q3 revenue level. The macro-to-Upstart transmission is a proxy; Upstart has not commented since the hike.

findings.finding: Per-day originations accelerated through the quarter rather than fading: July $51.0m/day, August $50.7m/day, September $53.1m/day, the best of Q3 even though September included the post-hike weeks. The UMI read 1.49 on 2026-10-05, at the guide's 1.50 assumption, so the macro input the company guides on has not deteriorated. This is the counterweight to finding 2 for the Q4 commentary and the October number.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Monthly origination releases began in 2026, so there is no print history on exit-rate commentary as such. Q2 2026's call flagged a July slowdown (34% YoY growth vs 50% in Q2), and the stock drifted down afterwards.
findings.why_not_priced: Aggregator coverage quoted only the quarterly total ($4.12bn, down q/q) and missed the rising per-day run-rate into September. If the exit rate were priced, the stock would not have fallen another 10% from the Oct 9 $24.10 close to $21.69 with no new company news.
findings.independence: August figures at https://www.securities.io/upstart-august-2026-originations-hit-1342-1-million-as-umi-holds-at-1-50/ and July at https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260803158614/en/upstart-publishes-july-2026-originations-and-latest-umi/. All are the company's own monthly releases, so this is one family of documents and the same data as finding 1 read at a different angle (exit rate, not quarter total).

findings.finding: Peers that reported after Upstart last spoke show benign consumer credit and strong unsecured-loan demand. SoFi Q3 2026 personal-loan originations were a record $12.6bn (+69% YoY) with charge-offs down 34bp to 2.26%. Enova's NCO ratio fell to 8.1% from 8.5%. Happen (ex-LendingClub) beat, raised FY EPS to $1.87-1.92, and rose about 12% on 2026-10-29 ('we continue to outperform on credit'). OneMain's NCO rose modestly to 7.24% from 7.00%. Benign credit supports the loss curves Upstart's funding partners buy on and the contribution-margin path.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Credit-driven reactions: Nov 2025 -14.8% when the model 'overreacted' to macro and cut volume. No positive print has been credited to credit alone.
findings.why_not_priced: UPST fell into these peer prints rather than rallying with Happen's +12%. If the benign credit read had transferred, UPST would not be at its 52-week low the week after. The market is treating UPST's problem as volume and take rate, not credit, so this finding is small.
findings.independence: Happen: https://www.tikr.com/blog/happen-soars-12-on-earnings-beat-and-raised-outlook-we-continue-to-outperform-on-credit. Enova: https://finviz.com/news/406876/enova-reports-third-quarter-2026-results. OneMain counter-data: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001584207/000158420726000041/omf-20260930.htm. These are separate documents but all proxies; Pagaya's release (finding 2) points the other way on take rate.

findings.finding: Short interest is 26.9m shares, 33.4% of float, 6.4 days to cover (FINRA record date 2026-10-15), with the stock at its 52-week low, 57% off the high and -10.9% over 20 days into the print. findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The one up-reaction in the last seven, Feb 2025, was +31.8%. The right tail on this name is large when the short base is caught.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price. The finding is that the downside the +16.8 skew pays for has to get past a short base about 6 days of volume deep, and shorts have already begun trimming (-5.9% in the last period). The option market's lean is on the same side as the shorts, which is why the right tail is underpriced if the guide holds.

findings.finding: 8-K of 2026-10-20: on 2026-10-16 Upstart Network entered a $200m senior secured 364-day revolver with MUFG at Term SOFR + 3.00%. It is secured on substantially all assets, carries covenants (minimum liquidity $100m, secured leverage of at most 2.5x), and is explicitly for general purposes and 'to fund the initial capitalization of Upstart Bank'. It matures 45 days after the bank's initial capitalization and is repaid from affiliate loan sales to the bank.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on a corporate facility; the bank charter (OCC conditional approval, July 2026) produced a +5.8% day on the announcement.
findings.why_not_priced: The quiet 8-K drew no wire coverage found. What the money buys: capitalizing Upstart Bank, which is corroborated by the conditional OCC approval and the early-2027 launch target, so this is not distress. Against that, borrowing secured to capitalize the bank, after $100m of H1 buybacks, says corporate cash is tight, and the bank is a cost centre with no 2026 revenue. Net zero; it resolves on the call if management updates bank timing, FDIC/Fed approvals or the 2027 expense line.

baseline_tension: The negatives (revenue gap to consensus, pressure on the FY guide) agree with the +16.8 put skew and the slide to a 52-week low, so they are probably largely priced. The positives (rising September run-rate, benign peer credit, 33% of float short) cut against the skew. That is why the findings net to about zero, and why p_up sits only 5 points below 50 on the reaction history rather than lower.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (crowded short, 33.4% of float, against a negative; negative agrees with the skew so likely priced): shrank the reported-quarter revenue finding from -1.0 to -0.75 and the guidance finding from -2.5 to -2.0, once each.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the MUFG $200m revolver funds the bank capitalization, a use corroborated by the conditional OCC approval and early-2027 launch, so it was moved from -0.25 to 0.0.
Lesson 5 (proxy transmission filed small, not dropped): the Pagaya take-rate read and the Fed path stay inside finding 2, labelled as proxy in independence.
Lesson 6 (verify the bar): the bar is confirmed by two agreeing sources ($365.5m Benzinga, $364.63m Earnings Whispers); no cap needed.
Lesson 1 (reaction veto): left p_up at 45 and abs_move at 13; this name sells beats (Q2 2026 -0.4% then drift), so no finding was enlarged on the fundamental read.
